maxArray (vericoding dv0154)

This page describes one task for the t checker.

Problem: /* This task involves identifying the maximum value in a non-empty array of integers. The objective is to determine which element in the array is greater than or equal to every other element, ensuring that the selected value is one of the elements in the array. -----Input----- The input consists of: • a: An array of integers. It is assumed that the array is non-empty (i.e., its size is at least 1). -----Output----- The output is an integer that represents the maximum element in the array. This value is guaranteed to satisfy the following: • It is greater than or equal to every element in the array. • It is exactly equal to one of the elements in the array. -----Note----- It is assumed that the provided array is non-empty. In cases where the array is empty, the function's behavior is not defined. */

car race collision

An exercise from the t practice set.

Problem: Imagine a road that's a perfectly straight infinitely long line. n cars are driving left to right; simultaneously, a different set of n cars are driving right to left. The two sets of cars start out being very far from each other. All cars move in the same speed. Two cars are said to collide when a car that's moving left to right hits a car that's moving right to left. However, the cars are infinitely sturdy and strong; as a result, they continue moving in their trajectory as if they did not collide. This function outputs the number of such collisions.

Signature: humaneval_dafny_041_car_race_collision__car_race_collision(int) -> int

Example: humaneval_dafny_041_car_race_collision__car_race_collision(22) == 484

Example: humaneval_dafny_041_car_race_collision__car_race_collision(23) == 529

A task written for dawnr's exercise pages.

Implement this specification in t.

gate recursion
task verus_examples_recursion_compute_arith_sum__compute_arith_sum(n: int) returns (sum: int)
  requires n >= 0
  requires n < 100
  ensures sum >= 0
  ensures arith_sum_int(n) == sum
spec fun arith_sum_int(i: int): int
  decreases i
= if i <= 0 then 0 else i + arith_sum_int(i - 1)

Loops in t

A while loop in t names its invariants and a decreases expression. The invariants must hold before the loop and after every iteration, and the decreases expression must shrink.

Sequences in t

A seq holds integers. len(s) is its length and s[i] its element at i, defined for i in [0, len(s)). Sequences compare by value.

Specifications in t

A task states what it requires of its inputs and what it ensures of its result. A program meets its specification when every run that satisfies the requires ends with the ensures true.

Example lines

An Example line names the task, its arguments and the expected result, such as Example: f(3) == 9. The t tool runs the program on each line.

Near-miss programs

A twin is a program with one deliberate edit, such as an off-by-one or a negated condition, and an input at which it answers differently.

Divisors

A divisor of n divides n with no remainder. Every n greater than one has at least two divisors, one and itself.

Strings as sequences

A string reaches a t program as a seq of character codes, so the string ab is the sequence [97, 98].

Booleans

true and false are values of type bool; t never treats a bool as a number.
